provenance_note: Expected inflow, rising-main size, required pump flow and head, duty point, sump useful volume, worst-case starts, input power and rule flags were computed by bench-src/ref/gen_plbliftstation.py, an independent Python implementation written from the published method (_plb/lift/METHOD.md: EN 12056-2 Qww = K·√ΣDU, EN 12056-4 velocity 0.7–2.3 m/s and minimum DN, Darcy–Weisbach with Colebrook solved by scipy brentq, pump parabola intersection by brentq, V = Qp·Tc/4, EN 12056-4:2000 §6.3 T·Qp (Table 5), V > rising-main volume and V ≥ 20 l, §5.1 surface water not mixed with domestic wastewater), not from the page code. Pipe series dimensions are input data from EN 12201-2, EN ISO 1452-2 and EN 10255. Consistency with METHOD + 10 external anchors worked by hand from the cited formulas (EN 12056-2 Qww = K·√ΣDU and the largest-DU floor, EN 12056-4 0.7 m/s on PE d90, sump V = Qp·Tc/4, Darcy–Weisbach with the Swamee–Jain friction factor, closed-form duty point on a fittings-dominated main, DIN 1986-100 ramp rain at r(5,100) 600 l/(s·ha) as a separate surface-water plant, EN 12056-4 §5.1 mixed streams, §6.3 20 l minimum and volume greater than the rising main); the generator refuses to write the reference unless its model reproduces the anchors. No published manufacturer sizing example was available to the author, so none is claimed.
